svg.text: Figure C — Trust boundaries and threat model
Only tier 1 is enforced by cryptography. Tier 2 is now enforced against the operator but sits downstream of tier 3. Tier 3 is bounded trust, not an absence of trust.
TIER 1 — CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY GUARANTEED
Holds against a fully malicious operator. No trust required. Verified on-chain; tampering rejected (4/4 soundness checks).
Calibration-head execution
halo2/KZG proof, 2^15 rows
verifyProof = 684,696 gas
prove 2.09 s · proof 17.4 KB
Guarantees: given logit L,
head(vk) maps L → attested c
+ conformal set, in-circuit (Phase B)
Slash arithmetic
BrierMath, WAD fixed point
no unchecked blocks; 543 gas
monotonicity + properness fuzzed
Guarantees: slash is exactly
stake·(c−o)², capped, no overflow
same arithmetic drives the reputation EMA
NOT covered by tier 1
• the base classifier (not in circuit)
• provenance of the input logit L
• truthfulness of the applicant features
• SHAP + counterfactual (hash-committed only)
• the fitted constants T and conformal q
A fabricated L yields a valid proof.
ThreatModel.t.sol::test_tier1_marginIsUnverified…
CONTENT INTEGRITY ONLY — ModelRegistry (Phase G)
Guarantees the artifact behind a version id hashes to the recorded value, so substitution is detectable by anyone. It is a cryptographic
property, but a narrow one, so it does not sit in tier 1: it says nothing about execution or training.
Does NOT establish that training was honest, nor that the registered artifact is the one that actually ran.
ModelRegistry.t.sol::test_boundary_poisonedModelRegistersAndVerifiesCleanly
TIER 2 — ECONOMICALLY ASSUMED
Holds if the operator is rational and the assumption is enforced in code. Both now are — but enforcement is subordinate to tier 3.
Assumption A — honest confidence reporting
Brier is strictly proper, so expected loss is minimised at the
operator's true belief: E[slash] = S((c−p)² + p(1−p)).
Verified numerically against the deployed Solidity at p = 0.3, 0.7.
STATUS: enforced by the payoff structure —
but only for decisions that are actually disputed, and only if
dispute selection is independent of the reported c.
BrierMath.t.sol::test_properScoringRule_honestyIsOptimal
Assumption B — stake is available when slashed
STATUS: ENFORCED (Phase 3a). Was broken in v0.
Two-step requestWithdrawal / executeWithdrawal behind an
unbonding delay; any open dispute freezes execution.
Residual gap A: an operator never disputed inside the
window exits intact — a bound on the dispute window, not the lock.
Residual gap B: the freeze is released by RESOLUTION,
which is a tier-3 action. Tier 2 is subordinate to tier 3.
TIER 3 — BOUNDED TRUST (no cryptographic or economic guarantee)
An N-of-M committee decides who loses money. N colluding members can decide it arbitrarily. Smaller red region than v0 — same colour.
Dispute outcome
resolveDispute — N of M resolvers
Improvement: one key no longer suffices.
N colluding = v0's single admin exactly.
Admin appoints and can replace the
committee, so the bound covers resolution,
not selection. Resolvers stake nothing.
No evidentiary standard. No appeal.
test_tier3_nOfMCollusionHasSameEffectAsV0Admin
Ground truth for a loan rejection
The counterfactual is unobservable: a
rejected applicant never demonstrates
repayment. "The decision was wrong" has
no on-chain referent.
Unsolved — not merely unimplemented.
Moving from one voter to N voters does
not create a fact that did not exist.
Operator reputation (Phase F)
EMA of realised Brier score, updated at
each resolution. Aggregation is on-chain
and auditable — anyone can replay it.
But its INPUTS are tier-3 outcomes, so it
sits in tier 3 and inherits that trust.
On-chain ≠ zk-proved. A colluding
committee can manufacture any score.
test_tierBoundary_colludingCommitteeCanManufacture…
BELOW TIER 3 — GNN collusion detection wired to enforcement (Phase E + CollusionOracle)
One reporter key relays an unvalidated model whose false-positive rate on real traffic has never been measured. Thinner than tier 3: the committee needs N signatures, this needs one.
An enforced flag blocks the claimant from disputing and quarantines their payout. It CANNOT slash: the operator penalty is unchanged and still requires the committee.
Containment: appeal window before any effect (zero-length rejected at construction) · quarantine refunded in full on clearing · forfeiture is a separate admin-only act.
A false positive silences a legitimate claimant, and thereby protects a bad decision.
test_dangerous_falsePositiveSilencesAnHonestClaimant · recommended posture: attach address(0)
Cheapest attack today (still requires breaking no cryptography)
1. Attest with a valid proof over a fabricated logit — tier 1 does not bind L. 2. Failing that, corrupt N committee members (tier 3) and resolve favourably,
which also unfreezes the exit via residual gap B. 3. Or compromise the single reporter key and flag the claimants. Cryptographic work: still none.
